detailed_results.raw_thinking:
We are given: "For each integer $n \ge 10$, let $X_n=2\mathbb{CP}^2\# n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$, where $\#$ denotes connected sum and $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ is $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with the opposite orientation. Let $T(X_n)$ denote the Torelli group of $X_n$, i.e. the subgroup of the mapping class group (smooth isotopy classes of diffeomorphisms of $X_n$) consisting of classes represented by diffeomorphisms continuously isotopic to the identity. Which statement holds for $T(X_n)$?"

The answer choices are:

(A) There exists a single surjective homomorphism $\Phi:T(X_n)\to \mathbb{Z}^\infty$ for all sufficiently large $n$, but not necessarily for every $n\ge 10$.

(B) For every $n\ge 10$, there exists a homomorphism $\Phi:T(X_n)\to \mathbb{Z}^\infty$ whose image has infinite rank, but which need not be surjective onto $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$.

(C) For every $n\ge 10$, there exists a surjective homomorphism $\Phi:T(X_n)\to \mathbb{Z}^\infty$, where $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ is the direct sum of countably infinitely many copies of $\mathbb{Z}$.

(D) For every $n\ge 10$, there exists a homomorphism $\Phi:T(X_n)\to \mathbb{Z}^\infty$ with infinite image.

(E) For every $n\ge 10$, every diffeomorphism of $X_n$ that is continuously isotopic to the identity determines, via the families Seiberg--Witten construction, a surjective homomorphism $T(X_n)\to \mathbb{Z}^\infty$.

Interpretation: We are dealing with 4-manifolds: $X_n = 2\mathbb{CP}^2 \# n \overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$. That is the connected sum of two copies of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and n copies of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ (the complex projective plane with opposite orientation, i.e., the same as a smooth manifold but with opposite orientation, so it has signature -1). So $X_n$ is a simply connected smooth 4-manifold. Its intersection form: $\mathbb{CP}^2$ has intersection form $(1)$, and $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ has intersection form $(-1)$. So $2\mathbb{CP}^2$ gives $(1) \oplus (1)$, and $n\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ gives $(-1)^n$.
